incident-bot: HIGH SEV: Customer 'Argos Systems' (dedicated-vpc-arg-01) experiencing 5xx spike on inference endpoints (p99 latency > 5s) — paging oncall
Maya (oncall): acked. jumping in. pulling logs now.
Maya (oncall): seeing a lot of `503` from runtime serving on pool node g4-02, KV cache misses skyrocketed.
Chris: which pool is that? Argos is on dedicated pool `argos-pool-1` pinned to g4 instances, right?
Maya (oncall): yes. node list: `g4-01,g4-02,g4-03`. traffic skewed to g4-02 (80%).
Sylvia: I can take runtime side — will check kernel crashes / OOM logs.
Maya (oncall): copying logs: ```ERROR runtime: failed to allocate kv cache slot: out of memory
[2026-03-15T15:04:11Z] inference request id=... status=503```
Tomas: could be a bad prefix-cache blowup from recent customer dataset? Any large system prompt changes?
Maya (oncall): Argos reported switching to a new prompt template at 15:00 UTC. rolling rate from 50rps -> 120rps.
Emily (CS): I just pinged Argos support lead — they're seeing high latency in their app. They're on standby for any traffic shift.
Chris: immediate mitigation: move `argos-pool-1` traffic to warm spare pool `dedicated-warm-2` to reduce load on g4-02, and cordon g4-02 for investigation.
Maya (oncall): initiating route override: `redwood route set --customer argos --pool dedicated-warm-2 --duration 30m`
incident-bot: action logged by Maya (oncall): route override created (id: r-8721).
Sylvia: cordoning g4-02 now: `kubectl drain node g4-02 --ignore-daemonsets` — evicting 12 serving pods.
Chris: spinning up a replacement node in the pool (g4-04) to restore capacity.
Maya (oncall): monitoring p99 — down from 5.2s to 0.8s after traffic shift. good.
Emily (CS): looping in Raj and Mike for customer comms and legal/SLA flag. Argos is enterprise with an SLA >99.9%.
Raj (Sales): thanks. we need a quick exec note for Argos CSM + AM. they want ETA and whether credits are required.
Mike (Legal): flagging contract review — potential SLA credit exposure if incident > threshold. collect timeline and affected window.
Maya (oncall): current incident window: 15:00 UTC (traffic change) -> 15:22 UTC (route override applied) — ~22 minutes of elevated errors.
Sylvia: root cause so far: combination of sudden prompt-induced KV cache growth on g4-02 causing OOMs and request queuing skew; autoscaler didn't add nodes because pool was at max reserved capacity (customer dedicated).
Tomas: follow-up mitigation: add adaptive eviction for prefix cache and an emergency autoscale override for dedicated pools (customers with >= reserved capacity ok to burst to warm pools).
Chris: file an infra change ticket for autoscale override within 24h. for now, patch runtime to reject extremely large system prompts that would trigger unbounded KV growth — temporary guard.
Emily (CS): drafting customer message — will post here for review. first pass: "We observed elevated errors and latency starting at 15:00 UTC due to a sudden high-volume prompt and cache growth on a node in your dedicated pool. We shifted traffic to a warm pool at 15:22 UTC which restored service. We're continuing an RCA and will propose credits if SLA hit."
Raj (Sales): suggest adding: "We recommend a short-term workaround: pinning requests to a broader pool and avoid the new prompt template until confirmed."
Mike (Legal): fine, keep wording non-admissional: state facts, timeline, mitigation, and next steps; don't promise credit amount until review.
Maya (oncall): note: we preserved logs and request ids (attached to ticket INC-8721) and snapshot of KV cache metrics.
Sylvia: opened follow-up RCA ticket INC-8721-RCA assigned to Chris/Tomas. estimated 72h completion.
Tomas: I'll start the RCA — steps: reproduce with Argos prompt, measure KV growth, evaluate patch to prefix eviction, and propose autoscale config.
Chris: ops followup: create canary for TTL-based KV eviction and run against dedicated-warm-2 before rolling to dedicated pools.
Emily (CS): finalizing customer comm now. will send to Argos at 16:05 UTC with current timeline and next check-in at 24h.
Raj (Sales): if Argos asks for credits, we'll propose a standard credit equivalent to X% pro-rated for the 22m window; need finance to approve but we can offer to route to legal/finance.
Mike (Legal): will review contract and SLA formula; please attach metric window and error rates.
Maya (oncall): closing loop: monitoring steady. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved — keeping thread for RCA and comm artifacts. :white_check_mark:
Emily (CS): thanks everyone. I'll paste the final customer-facing note here after sending so we have a record.
Chris: also scheduling a post-incident review with eng/runtime, ops, and cs tomorrow 14:00 UTC.
Tomas: adding action items to INC-8721-RCA: repro, patch, autoscale policy, customer comm draft, exec summary.
Maya (oncall): handed off to Chris and Tomas for RCA. Maya out.
incident-bot: incident status changed to MONITORED -> HANDOFF, assigned: Chris, Tomas.
